meaning: A teasing headline or picture made to make you click. The story behind it is often disappointing.
clues: It is made to catch your eye.
It teases you and leaves out the key facts on purpose.
You have to click to find out more, and the story often turns out to be a letdown.
Titles like "You won't believe what happened next!" are classic examples.
It is one word with nine letters and starts with C.
assumes: A poster is a large printed sheet hung on a wall
A banner ad is an ad strip on a web page
A spoiler gives away the ending of a story

decoys.meaning: A large printed sheet hung on a wall to show an event, a movie, or a message.
A long, thin ad that sits across the top or side of a web page.
A hint or fact that gives away how a movie, book, or show ends.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: Back in my day, the papers at the grocery checkout did the same trick. "Alien Baby Found!" Every week!

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Tip: if a headline sounds too wild, see whether a news site you trust reports the same story.
